objective_and_hypothesis.justification: This matches the Score 3 description: the study states a testable objective concerning introductions, persistence, and climatic/travel drivers, and explicitly links its sequential surveillance, phylogenetic, and modeling methods to those questions and their public-health importance.
objective_and_hypothesis.quote: In this study, we combined case surveillance, virus sequencing, and transmission dynamic modeling to estimate the dynamics and drivers of DENV in Florida from 2009 to 2024.

public_health_relevance.justification: This matches the Score 3 description because it addresses documented dengue outbreaks in Miami-Dade and Florida, including the 2022–2024 consecutive outbreaks, in the context of the major dengue surge in the Americas.
public_health_relevance.quote: From 2022 to 2024, consecutive outbreaks in Miami-Dade County were mainly caused by a single lineage of dengue virus (DENV) serotype 3

study_design_rigor.justification: This matches the Score 3 description: the paper details surveillance sources, sequencing protocols, genomic filtering, phylogeography, climate-index construction, and Bayesian models; it also provides GenBank accessions, a code repository, and sensitivity analyses excluding 2023–2024 and Miami-Dade.
study_design_rigor.quote: All code and model results are available at: https://github.com/EmmaTS22/dengueFL.

results_and_conclusion.justification: This matches the Score 2 description: extensive figures, tables, phylogenetic analyses, models, and limitations support generally cautious conclusions, but reporting is inconsistent. The text reports 594 local cases and 329 Miami-Dade cases, while Figure 1C's displayed county counts sum to 592 and label Miami-Dade as 327; Figure 3's caption also reverses the contents of panels A and B. No discrete count was reported as a decimal or fraction.
results_and_conclusion.quote: From 2009 through 2024, there were a total of 594 local dengue cases reported from 15 counties

references.justification: The references provide a balanced subject-relevant mix of foundational dengue and vector literature, recent dengue surveillance and climate studies, Florida outbreak reports, genomic-sequencing methods, and appropriate phylogenetic/statistical methodology sources. The list includes a small number of preprints, but these are supplemented by many peer-reviewed Lancet, Nature, PLoS, CDC/PAHO, and methodological sources; no clearly unrelated reference was identified.
references.quote: G. Paz-Bailey, L. E. Adams, J. Deen, K. B. Anderson, L. C. Katzelnick, Dengue. Lancet 403, 667–682 (2024).
